claim.quote: A narrow $J^{PC} = 1^{++}$ signal is observed in the $f_0(980)\,\pi$ channel.

key_value.note: Mass of the new a1(1420) as quoted in the abstract.
key_value.quote: We identify a new $a_1$ meson with mass $(1414^{+15}_{-13})$ MeV/$c^2$ and width $(153^{+8}_{-23})$ MeV/$c^2$.

name: COMPASS observation of a new narrow axial-vector meson a1(1420)

summary.plain: In pion-proton diffractive scattering COMPASS saw a narrow new signal that is a previously unseen axial-vector meson, the a1(1420), with a mass of about 1.41 GeV. It decays only to a f0(980) and a pion, which hints at an exotic nature.
summary.technical: Partial-wave analysis (88 waves) of diffractive dissociation of 190 GeV/c pions into pi-pi-pi+ on a hydrogen target: a narrow J^PC = 1++ signal in the f0(980) pi channel, interpreted as a new a1 meson with mass 1414 +15 -13 MeV/c^2 and width 153 +8 -23 MeV/c^2, decaying only into f0(980) pi among the final states investigated.

title: Observation of a new narrow axial-vector meson a1(1420)
why_it_matters: A new light meson candidate that does not fit the ordinary quark-antiquark spectrum cleanly is a test case for exotic hadrons and for the role of rescattering effects.
